title: Google withdraws new Earth AI tool after warnings over misinformation risks
facts: Google paused an AI tool in Google Earth that enabled users to generate synthetic imagery over satellite views.
Google suspended the Nano Banana 2 image generator feature within 48 hours of its launch.
Google announced the integration of the Nano Banana 2 image generator into Google Earth on Thursday.
The retracted Google Earth feature permitted text-prompted modifications over aerial and 3D map data.
BBC Verify created synthetic images of a collapsed Eiffel Tower using the Google Earth AI tool.
Misinformation researcher Henk van Ess demonstrated the tool by creating fictitious images of an Iranian nuclear site.
Henk van Ess generated synthetic imagery depicting a non-existent hospital with bomb damage in Gaza.
Google embeds invisible watermarks into images created by its generative AI tools.
Users can verify image authenticity using Google's Gemini chatbot application and Lens tool.
BBC Verify demonstrated that Gemini could be misled into validating fake Google Earth images as real.
External AI detection tools occasionally failed to identify imagery generated by Google Earth's AI feature.
Henry Ajder is an AI detection researcher who analyzed the risks of synthetic satellite imagery.
BBC Verify successfully bypassed Google Earth content restrictions using adjusted text prompts.
Bill Greer serves as a geospatial analyst and co-founder of the non-profit satellite organization Common Space.
Bill Greer warned that synthetic satellite imagery undermines public confidence in verifiable overhead data.
